title: Hardware: the new configuration reads no level
summary: The station configuration was rebuilt offline from a template. LT-303 reads 0 % although the tank is partly full, and the fault lamp is on. Check the configuration against the drawing.
objectives: Match an analog channel's mode to the device
Explain why a 2-wire transmitter needs a supplied current input
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    StartPB : BOOL; (* Start button S1, normally open. *)
    StopPB : BOOL; (* Stop button S2, normally closed: TRUE while not pressed. *)
    LevelHigh : BOOL; (* High level switch LSH-305: TRUE when wet. *)
    InletOpen : BOOL; (* Inlet valve XV-301 open limit switch. *)
    InletClosed : BOOL; (* Inlet valve XV-301 closed limit switch. *)
    LevelRaw : INT; (* LT-303, 4-20 mA, 2-wire: generic profile 0..10000 = 0..100 %. *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    InletValve : BOOL; (* Inlet valve XV-301 solenoid. *)
    RunLamp : BOOL; (* Green lamp H1: filling with the inlet valve open. *)
    FaultLamp : BOOL; (* Red lamp H2: level invalid or high level. *)
    LevelOut : INT; (* Level retransmitted to the control room, 0..10000 = 0..100 %. *)
    LevelPercent : REAL; (* Level from LT-303, 0..100 %. *)
END_VAR
VAR
    LevelValid : BOOL; (* The level measurement is plausible: above 2 % and within range. *)
    Filling : BOOL; (* Fill request latch. *)
END_VAR
(* The program passed its factory test; this lab is about the station hardware. *)
LevelPercent := INT_TO_REAL(LevelRaw) / 100.0;
LevelValid := (LevelRaw > 200) AND (LevelRaw <= 10000);
(* Filling starts only from the valve's start position (closed and confirmed). *)
Filling := ((StartPB AND InletClosed) OR Filling) AND StopPB AND NOT LevelHigh AND LevelValid AND LevelPercent < 80.0;
InletValve := Filling;
RunLamp := Filling AND InletOpen;
FaultLamp := NOT LevelValid OR LevelHigh;
LevelOut := LevelRaw;
END_PROGRAM
instructions: The PLC runs the accepted program. Let the simulation run, press Start and confirm the symptom.
Open the Hardware tab: compare the configured (project) station with the detected one, then follow the signals.
Select a module for its channels, power and diagnostics; measure terminals with the multimeter.
Diagnose, repair (configuration labs: correct the configuration in Advanced mode and download it), then verify.
hints: Which signal type does the drawing show for LT-303?
A voltage input cannot tell a dead loop from an empty tank.

troubleshooting.symptom: The tank does not fill and the fault lamp is on. LT-303 reads 0 %, but the sight glass shows about 20 %.

debrief.rootCause: The LT-303 channel was configured as a 0-10 V voltage input, but LT-303 is a 2-wire 4-20 mA transmitter. A voltage input does not supply the loop, so the transmitter had no power, the input saw 0 V and reported a valid-looking 0 %. The program's plausibility check rejected the level and blocked filling.
evidence: The drawing shows LT-303 as a 2-wire 4-20 mA transmitter.
The channel was configured for 0-10 V, and the Compare view reported the mode mismatch.
The input read 0 with good quality: a voltage input has no live zero to detect the dead loop.
debrief.repair: Configure channel 0 of the analog input module for 4-20 mA with diagnostics and loop supply, download the configuration, then compare the level with the sight glass.
debrief.reasoning: Configure every analog channel for the signal its device delivers, and for current inputs decide who powers the loop. A 4-20 mA live zero makes a dead loop visible; a 0-10 V channel cannot.
